claim: In W2, interpolation of the complete hidden-to-hidden matrix toward its initialization during updates 5–8, with trained input weights, biases and a fresh readout held fixed, increased oracle-referenced prefix-function loss over the predeclared dose grid. In at least eight of ten fresh seeds, the trapezoidal excess exceeded that of every one of 32 block-norm-matched random paths and reached at least one quarter of the paired prefix-loss advantage over F-INIT. The intact trained cores also outperformed the prefix-blind reference. This supports a bounded causal contribution of the trained hidden-to-hidden parameters to accurate prefix-dependent prediction under the specified intervention and fixed surrounding computation. It does not establish monotonicity, selectivity over continuation processing, localized content, necessity, or a uniquely identified mechanism.
